subject.title: fix(gateway): enforce plugin-ownership check in sessions.patch

question: Should plugin-runtime callers fail closed when `sessions.patch` targets a legacy persisted row with no `pluginOwnerId`?
rationale: Unknown ownership cannot be safely assigned to a plugin, but unconditional rejection can break previously tolerated plugin workflows after upgrade, so this compatibility/security boundary needs explicit owner intent.

options.title: Reject ownerless rows
options.body: Treat absent ownership as no plugin authority and leave those rows manageable only by operators or non-plugin clients.

options.title: Add temporary compatibility
options.body: Preserve a narrowly documented legacy path until an explicit migration or adoption mechanism is designed.

options.title: Defer ownerless policy
options.body: Land explicit foreign-owner rejection now and handle legacy ownerless rows in separate canonical work.

recommendation.title: Reject ownerless rows
recommendation.body: Treat absent ownership as no plugin authority and leave those rows manageable only by operators or non-plugin clients.

likelyOwner.reason: The current session patch projection and storage-neutral accessor boundary were introduced in this person's recent commit, making them the strongest available owner for the ordering and upgrade-policy choice.
